  "text": "Tobias Reel came down the church road in the morning because there was no other road to come down.\n\nThe gulls were back. The sea had its colour again, which was no colour, which was the colour it had always been.\n\nHe did not go to the beach. He went along the top of the dune, where the grass was, and from there he could see the eleven posts standing in a line with the water well below them, and not one of them moving.\n\nThe house was shut. The door was latched; he could see the lip of the latch from the path. The front window was grey. There was a lamp on the sill, and it was not lit, and he had known it would not be, and he looked at it a long while anyway.\n\nHe thought of knocking. His hand came up and he put it back in his coat.\n\nOn the path, the lantern hung from its nail and did not ring. He touched the glass. It was cold the way glass is cold, no more.\n\nWhen he turned to go, he turned toward the water, because he was an old man and his knees chose for him.
